label: 1-3 steps after an early r in the original sequence
explanation: Fires in the original-input phase on the 1-3 steps that follow an input of the letter r, as long as the current step is early (t <= 5). It is a short-lived trace of a recent r. prev_tok == r has 15.8x lift and prev2_tok == r has 13.5x. Activation is weak on the step right after an r at position 0 (about 0.17 of max) and strongest around t = 2-4. It is largest when several r tokens appear in a row at the start (e.g. r r r X peaks at X, near max), and it decays over the next 2-3 steps. It does not fire at t = 0, almost never fires during the copy phase (0 activations) and only weakly at the delimiter. It also does not fire after an r that occurs late in the sequence (t >= 6), which is the main source of false positives for an unrestricted window. The input token itself does not matter. Dev split: P 0.85, R 0.89, F1 0.87, mass recall 0.98.

issues: Minor: the third step after an r (rel_tok(-3)==r with no r at -1 or -2) is not reliable. Precision is 0.55-0.71 by t, it covers only 5.7% of activation mass, and it accounts for most of the 25k false positives. Without it the predicate scores P 0.92, R 0.75, F1 0.825, mass recall 0.92, so keeping it is still the better trade. The '1-3 steps' wording slightly overstates step 3.
Minor: the t<=5 cutoff is soft. prev_tok==r at t=5 has precision 0.59 and at t=6 has 0.09, so the decay is gradual, not a hard edge.

Missed activations are mostly scattered near-zero values (about 0.01 of max) plus weak delimiter firing after a recent r. Together they hold 2.0-2.1% of mass, and they agree with the claim that the feature fires only weakly at the delimiter.

Checked claims: copy phase has 0 active steps. t=0 has 0 active steps. prev_tok==r gives 15.8x lift and prev2_tok==r gives 13.5x. prev_tok==r at t=1-3 has precision about 1.0. prev_tok==r at t>=6 has precision 0.047. Current-token lift is flat at 1.1-1.3x. Test scores match what was reported (P 0.850, R 0.892, F1 0.871, mass recall 0.979).
